Overall verdict: Minor revision
The short paper is acceptable for the CICM 2026 presentation-only / mathematical-software-workshop route, provided the submission package is cleaned up before EasyChair. It is not trying to be a full proceedings-style software paper: the stated contribution is a compact “publication-coordinate” audit interface and bounded checker contract for AI-assisted formal-mathematics pipelines, with the worked newmath/automath case serving as illustration rather than as a full reproducibility claim. submission_abstract
For the two-page claim boundary, I do not see a rejection-level blocker. The paper explicitly limits the PDF claim to the bounded interface: finite rows determine which coordinates may be cited, while the PDF does not claim that every imported source object is semantically correct or freshly rebuilt on a clean machine. That boundary is exactly the right kind of limitation for a presentation-only short paper. submission_abstract The checker contract is also stated in reviewable terms: typed load-bearing pointers, a finite Horn-style transition relation, and explicit nonconsequences such as “bounded record-gate success” not implying artifact semantics, archive status, or venue acceptance. submission_abstract
The main revision needed is packaging clarity, not scientific scope. The PDF says the longer note, row schema, manifest, digest table, replay report, and review-bundle records live in the supplement, and later says the non-PDF supplement may be used to inspect those materials while the PDF claim remains compact. submission_abstract submission_abstract That is acceptable, but before EasyChair the authors should make the boundary operationally obvious: reviewers must be able to tell exactly which files are operative support material, which checker command or report corresponds to the bounded claim, and which material is merely contextual.
